claim.quote: Evidence of the Purely Leptonic Decay B- --> tau- nu_tau-bar

date.note: arXiv submission date (v1, 9 April 2006). Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 251802 (2006).

name: Evidence for the purely leptonic decay B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅
notes: The collaboration's word for this result is 'evidence' (in the title); it is not recorded as an observation.

significance.quote: We detect the signal with a significance of 3.5 standard deviations including systematics

summary.plain: Belle presented the first evidence that a B particle can decay straight into a tau lepton and a neutrino. Because a neutrino cannot be seen, events were selected by fully reconstructing one of the two B particles produced in each collision.
summary.technical: First evidence for B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅_τ in 414 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S) with 3.5σ significance, B = (1.79 ⁺⁰·⁵⁶₋₀.₄₉(stat) ⁺⁰·⁴⁶₋₀.₅₁(syst)) × 10⁻⁴, giving the first direct determination of the B decay constant f_B.

title: Evidence of the Purely Leptonic Decay B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅_τ
why_it_matters: In the Standard Model the decay proceeds via annihilation of the b and u quarks into a W boson; the paper notes that physics beyond the Standard Model, such as supersymmetry or two-Higgs-doublet models, could modify the branching fraction through a charged Higgs boson. The abstract says the measurement implies f_B = 0.229 +0.036/−0.031 (stat) +0.034/−0.037 (syst) GeV and 'is the first direct measurement of this quantity'.
